﻿<!-- pr-reviewer: 12d6359c8caac0186b839e4731505b5d0a8f528c -->
Read-only safety-floor review and quick pass (Opus, diff only, not built) of head 12d6359c8caac0186b839e4731505b5d0a8f528c.

Verdict: no blockers

## What I checked

I read the full diff, issue #1649 with its comments, AGENTS.md, `crates/ui/AGENTS.md`, and these files at the head: `crates/post/src/post/invert.rs`, `engine.rs` (the pass order), `wcs_rotate.rs` (`chunk_bounds`), the probing blocks of `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`, and `crates/app/src/posting.rs` (`op_streams_by` and the post entry points). I did not build and I did not run tests.

### 1. The mirror law

- One flipped X or Y: `translate_rules` negates the axis on moves, arc centres, cycle X/Y, `Start*`, `Origin*`, the stock box, the guard target and the probe target, expect value and back-off delta. The script computes `x - orgX`, so the posted word is `-(p - O)`. I/J follow from the mirrored centre and start.
- G2/G3 swap when the arc plane holds exactly one flipped axis (`in_plane`). This is correct for G17, G18 and G19. With X and Y flipped, G17 arcs do not swap and G18/G19 arcs swap. That is correct.
- G41/G42 swap when `f.x != f.y`. With X and Y flipped (a half turn), they do not swap. That is correct.
- Helix: the flip pass sets `helix: true`. A reflection keeps the Z travel and reverses the turn. This is correct, and `a_flipped_wcs_cuts_the_cam_path` pins it.
- Canned cycles: X/Y mirror. Z, R, peck, dwell and the cycle kind do not change, so the tap direction and G98/G99 do not change. A flipped Z is refused before the cycle law.
- A/B/C moves (3+2 tilt posts as `abc`) are refused by the mirror. Rotary, multi-axis, wire, EDM and turning operations are also refused at the app gate (`setup_wcs_flip::op_problem`). The post pass also refuses turning, EDM and plasma sections.
- Flip and WCS rotation: refused at the app gate (`offset_frame != Square`) and in the engine (`WcsYaw`). The flip pass runs first, so the two transforms never change one section.
- Flip and an inverted machine axis: the two mirrors compose. `a_flipped_axis_on_an_inverted_machine_axis_posts_the_standard_signs` pins this. The travel check multiplies the two signs the same way (`crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs:359`).
- G53, G28 and the tool-change position come from the machine values in the script, not from the stream. They are not mirrored. That is correct.
- Each mill, probe and turning section is written through the one `Dump` in `op_streams_by`, and the wire stream through `posting_wire.rs`. The two sites set `wcs_flip`. Thus no section of a flipped setup gets to the engine without `PARAM WcsFlip`.
- `chunk_bounds` ends a chunk at `ENDSECTION`, so the flip parameter and the moves of one section are in one chunk. The pass gives one record out for each record in, so the line map of the viewer stays correct.
- The work envelope and the travel check use the posted sign. Simulation, the gouge checks and generation stay in the setup frame. With the stated meaning (the controller reads that axis reversed), the physical cut is the simulated cut.

### 2. Other dialects

Only `fanuc.cps` and `haas.cps` declare `axisInversion = true`. Each other script is refused by name at two places: the verification gate (`setup_problem`: "its post (...) is not verified for a mirrored program") and the engine (`wcs_flip::apply`: "does not declare axisInversion = true"). This applies to carvera, doosan-dnm, fanuc-lathe, grblhal, heidenhain, mach4, mazak, sinker-iso, sinumerik, sodick-wire, tinyg, tormach, tormach-lathe, tormach-plasma and wire-iso. The lathe, plasma, wire and EDM scripts are also refused by the operation kind. I found no path that posts a flipped setup without the mirror.

### 3. Commands and undo

The logic of `SetWcsFlip` does not change (only its doc comment). The WCS page queues `CommandKind::SetWcsFlip`. The MCP tool calls the same command. The project file does not change in this PR (`flip` is from #1720). An unflipped stream stays byte-identical (`PARAM WcsFlip` is written only when a flag is set). Thus the `feat` title without `!` is correct.

### 4. Tests

- `crates/post/tests/wcs_flip.rs` pins arcs in the three planes, the helix, the compensation side, X+Y, the composition with an inverted machine axis, a mixed stream, the Z refusal, the rotation refusal, the refusal of 9 unverified scripts, bad `WcsFlip` values and the modal-origin refusal. Its Gate map line names `camcraft_post::post::wcs_flip`.
- `crates/app/tests/wcs_flip_post.rs` pins the mirrored program word by word, the gate refusals (Z, Mazak, rotation), generation without a change of the toolpath, the travel check, the setup sheet and the work envelope. Its Gate map line is present.
- `crates/app/tests/wcs_flip.rs` keeps the undo, delete-and-undo, project and MCP tests. Three tests of the old refusal are replaced by tests of the new behaviour in `wcs_flip_post.rs`.
- No test is `#[ignore]`d. No snapshot PNG changes. The `#[test]` count of `crates/ui` does not go down (two assertions change).
- Each test file is in the lowest crate that has its imports.

### 5. AGENTS.md

- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in non-test code of the diff.
- The layers are correct. The new post pass is in `camcraft-post`. The app files read the world. No new `camcraft-*` dependency.
- No file goes past 400 lines because of this PR. `invert.rs` has 371 lines. `posting.rs` (1589), `engine.rs` (616) and `post/mod.rs` (716) were already past the limit before this PR, and each grows by less than 10 lines.
- `docs/decisions/1649-wcs-flip-carry.md` has the README format. Each new module and test file has a provenance comment. I found no vendor text in the `.cps` lines or the docs.

### 6. Quick pass

- `git merge-tree` with `origin/main` (0ea577707) is clean.
- `crates/app/src/operation/heights.rs` is not in the diff. Line 128 (`.map(&resolve)`) is on main. Issue #2479 is open.
- The quick gate: the body names one red step (that clippy lint, which is on main). The body does not name the head sha of the gate run. The log name is `quick-20261118-074008` and the commit time is 10:02 UTC, so I cannot confirm that the run is on this head. I did not find the log.
- The body has what changed, the pinning tests, what was not exercised, a `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #1649`.
- The body has `Process change: yes (one row in the camcraft-mcp skill).` No tool in `xtask/` or the skills parses this line, and the reviewers look for the text, so a substring match finds it. A parser that reads the full line would not find it. Put `Process change: yes` on a line of its own.
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is not edited.
- The PR changes the note text in `wcs_page.rs`. The body has no before/after screenshots. `/merge-ready` does not offer a UI PR until the body has them.

## Findings (no blockers)

1. The meaning of a flip (the maintainer must confirm it). The PR reads a flip as "the controller reads that axis reversed" (the same law as an inverted machine axis, #374). On a controller where the axis is not reversed, the program cuts the mirror image of the part, and the simulation does not show this. The program note says `PROGRAM MIRRORED`. The WCS page note ("The posted program is mirrored on the flipped axis. Toolpaths do not change.") does not tell the user that the controller must run the axis reversed. The issue comment of 2026-11-17 expected that "a mirror changes climb milling into conventional milling". The decision file says the opposite and gives the reason. The code agrees with the decision file.
2. Probing with a work-offset write in a flipped setup (`fanuc.cps` `onProbeResult`, the `G10 L2` write). The #392 proof supports this, and that proof uses a machine-level reversal (the offset register is in reversed machine coordinates). If the control makes the flip with a mirror-image function and the machine coordinates stay standard, the correction goes in the wrong direction (an error of up to two times the tolerance). Follow-up: state the mechanism, or refuse `set_wcs` probing in a flipped setup until it is verified.
3. The WCS page note and the status line (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page.rs:180`, `crates/ui/src/state_wcs.rs:95`) say "mirrored" for a flipped and rotated WCS and for an unverified post. The post refuses these cases. Use `setup_wcs_flip::setup_problem` to select the note.
4. The MCP `refused` field (`crates/app/src/mcp/wcs_flip_tools.rs:64`) holds only `setup_problem`. It is `null` for a flipped X in a setup that has turning, rotary or tilted operations, but the gate refuses those (`op_problem`).
5. The travel check (`crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs:359`) also multiplies the lathe radius by the flip sign. The post refuses a lathe in a flipped setup, so the only result is an extra travel message. This is not a safety problem.
6. `crates/post/tests/wcs_flip.rs` tests the refusal of 9 of the 15 unverified scripts. The engine check is generic, so this is not a gap in the law.

## Follow-ups

- Findings 1 and 2: one `source:agent` issue for the flip meaning and probing (P3 if the maintainer says that a flip on his controller is a mirror-image function, else P7).
- Findings 3 and 4: one P7 issue.
- Before the merge: add screenshots to the body, put `Process change: yes` on a line of its own, and run a quick gate that names this head.
